newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian BFC says financial studies debate advances.
newsitem.headline: Belgian BFC says financial studies debate advances.

text.p: Belgium's regulatory Banking and Finance commission (BFC) says it is making progress with its study of the potential conflicts of interest when a broker publishes both a prospectus and financial study on an issuer.
An initial roundtable meeting of various parties concerned had produced a consensus on several points, BFC president Jean-Louis Duplat said on Wednesday.

One was that these studies "must distinguish between that which truly comes from the domain of financial analysis and that which tends to carry a judgement on the opportunity and the quality of the transaction," Duplat said.
His comments were made in the text of a speech presented at a seminar about the Brussels bourse and new growth markets, organised by Editions Laurence de Hemptinne.
He said it had been agreed that the editor of a prospectus must ensure subscribers were given access to all the objective information in the broker's financial analysis of a company.
If the broker's analysis contained forecasts on the issuer's medium-term prospects, and these were not in the prospectus, the study must clearly indicate the source of the data.

Duplat said there had been several recent cases of a financial intermediary bringing a company to the market and at the same time issuing a study with information that should have been in the prospectus or that needed further amplification.
